prompt: Design a high-fidelity landscape 16:10 desktop screenshot for Courrier, an email client. Show the real Inbox work surface, not a poster or a station photograph. This is the Split-flap arrivals-board challenger: a precise, dense message register with crisp fixed-width time cells, blackened deep charcoal panel, warm bone text and one amber signal color, restrained red only for an unread indicator. Layout: narrow left app rail listing exactly Boîte de réception, Feed, Paper, Réponse plus tard, Mis de côté, Brouillons, Corbeille; center pane with email rows showing sender, subject, preview, right-aligned time; wide right pane reading a selected email in readable normal body typography; a small top bar with Courrier mark on the left and account menu right, no search field. At bottom of reading pane put only compact actions Répondre, Réponse plus tard, Mettre de côté, Plus. Retain actual email semantics and a visible selected message. Make the list feel like a split-flap display through strict columns, subtle segmented number cells and letter spacing, not through mis-rendered random characters. Don’t invent route columns, counts, folders, attachments, people, charts, or actions. No giant display headline, station platform, travel motifs, photographs, physical board, telephone imagery or fake delivery statuses. The interface must still read as a useful email client with short, generic French demo content and highly legible hierarchy.
